config.port.description: Local port the extension listens on for the browser half. Must match the port in the Chrome extension's content.js.
config.maxTurns.description: Cap on turns in one run. 0 = no cap (default). One turn is one round trip to ChatGPT and takes tens of seconds. Runaway loops are already stopped elsewhere: two turns in a row with no tool call, or three in a row where every tool fails. This cap only catches "too long", and long work is not by itself wrong, so there is no default. Set 1 or more and it asks whether to keep going instead of stopping there.
config.allowlist.description: Commands that may run. Anything not listed is refused and the reason is sent back to ChatGPT. Commands do not go through a shell, so ; and | cannot be used to chain past this list.
config.denylist.description: Argument patterns (regular expressions) that are never auto-approved, even for an allowlisted command. These add to a built-in list that cannot be removed. Same idea as chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove in VS Code's own Chat and deniedCommands in Roo-Code.
config.requireRestorePoint.description: Refuse file edits and commands in a workspace where no checkpoint (a git commit) can be made. Off by default, like comparable extensions. Turn it on and nothing unrecoverable can be written.
config.loadGlobalRules.description: Include your global agent rules (~/.agents/AGENTS.md) and the list of available skills (~/.agents/skills) in the first message of a conversation. It adds about 17 KB to that first message, but saves restating the rules every time and saves a turn spent looking for a skill. The detailed rules (~/.agents/rules) and the skill bodies are not included; they are fetched on demand with read_rule / read_skill.
config.protectSecrets.description: Withhold the contents of files that look like they hold secrets (.env, keys, credentials). On by default: anything sent becomes part of a ChatGPT conversation and stays there, so the default errs toward not sending. Put a .bridgeignore in the workspace to add your own exclusions.
config.projectRulesLanguage.description: Language of the rules written into the ChatGPT project instructions. The 8,000-character limit counts characters, so a denser language fits more (measured: Traditional Chinese 2,812 / Japanese 3,592 / English 6,778 for the same rules). Default follows the panel language.
config.language.description: Interface language. The default, auto, follows the editor's display language, so you normally do not need to touch this. Set it only to use a different language from the editor.
config.subAgents.description: How many sub-agents may run at once. 0 disables them. Each sub-agent opens one more chatgpt.com tab.
config.subPortBase.description: First port used by sub-agents. They take consecutive ports from here.
config.revealOnStart.description: Open the conversation panel as soon as the editor starts. Useful for automated checks; off by default.
config.allowedOutside.description: Folders outside the workspace that may be touched. Choosing "always allow" adds the folder here. This is read access only; writing is governed by allowedOutsideWrite.
config.mcp.description: Borrow tools from MCP servers. Off by default: turning it on starts the configured servers' processes, so decide deliberately. Configuration is read from mcpServers in ~/.claude.json as-is, to avoid a second place to keep it. To disable a single server, add "disabled": true to it (the same shape Roo-Code and Claude Desktop use).
config.allowedOutsideWrite.description: Folders outside the workspace that may also be written to. Choosing "always allow" adds them here. Kept separate from read access (allowedOutside), because reading does little harm and writing cannot be undone.
config.allowedMcpServers.description: MCP servers you answered "always allow" for. Their tools run without asking. Kept separate from the command allowlist, because mixing them would let a server name act as an allowed command prefix.
config.allowedSites.description: Sites you answered "always allow" for (origins, in the form https://example.com). The browser tools open those sites without asking. Only the origin is remembered, not the path — paths multiply endlessly with ? and #, which would make remembering meaningless.
config.mode.description: Permission mode: how often to ask before acting.
config.outputStyle.description: Response style: pick a markdown file from ~/.claude/output-styles/ by its name. Empty means the default style.
config.requireModifierToSend.description: Send with Shift+Enter or Option+Enter instead of Enter. When off, Enter sends and the combinations insert a newline.
command.insertSelection.title: Add Selection to Chat
command.probeApis.title: Probe Real VS Code API Shapes (dev)
config.disabledTools.description: Tools to switch off. Empty by default (all available). All three reference implementations have the same shape (Configure Tools in VS Code's Chat, tool groups in Roo-Code, permissions in Claude Code). Finishing, asking, and reading skills cannot be switched off — without them the loop cannot end. For a blunt read-only setup, use the plan permission mode instead.
config.modes.description: Named roles. Each bundles an instruction with the tools it may not use. The model can request a switch with switch_mode; you approve it.
config.modes.slug: Short id the model names, e.g. architect
config.modes.name: Name shown when you are asked to approve the switch
config.modes.whenToUse: When this role fits. Shown to the model so it can pick
config.modes.instruction: How to work in this role. Handed over when the role starts
config.modes.disabledTools: Tools this role may not use, e.g. write_file

config.autosave.description: Save a file that has unsaved edits before reading or writing it. Off means the agent reads what is on disk, and your unsaved edits can overwrite its changes later.
config.respectGitIgnore.description: Skip files ignored by .gitignore when searching. Off means build output and dependencies are searched too.
config.preventDoneWithOpenTodos.descript: Push back once if it tries to finish while to-dos are still open. On by default: models forget the list they wrote themselves (measured: done went through with 1 of 5 items finished).

config.contextWindow.description: Assumed context window (in tokens) used only to show a percentage. 0 means no percentage — just the accumulated amount. The exact value cannot be read through the web UI, so it is not guessed for you.

config.commandTimeoutAllowlist.descripti: Command prefixes that never time out. A command starting with one of these is waited on until it finishes instead of being moved to the background (useful for builds and long test runs). An explicit timeout from the model still wins.

config.projectUrl.description: Where to start new conversations. Point it at a ChatGPT Project to have that project’s instructions apply (e.g. https://chatgpt.com/g/g-p-xxxx/project). Empty means plain chatgpt.com.
command.writeProjectInstructions.title: Write the Bridge Rules into a Project’s Instructions…
config.restartGapSeconds.description: How long to wait (in seconds) before re-creating a conversation. 0 waits not at all. Creating several in quick succession can get the whole account throttled.

config.diagnosticsAfterEdit.description: After an edit, report the problems that edit **added** (pre-existing ones are not reported).
command.startBrowser.title: Start the isolated browser
config.browserPath.description: Which browser the `browser_*` tools drive. Empty (the default) finds the browser you loaded the companion extension into, and falls back to the first Chromium-family browser installed. Set the full path to an executable to pin it.
config.browserProfile.description: The profile directory that browser runs on. Empty (the default) uses a dedicated one under Application Support, kept separate from the browser you use every day — the tools refuse to touch anything else. Change this only if you know what you are handing over.
config.thinking.description: Turn on ChatGPT thinking before sending. The toggle only appears when the open tab actually has that control and it responds — chatgpt.com has changed it three times since 2026-08, so this is detected, not assumed.
